1.41 Diagnose Cloud throughput and verify native query repairs

Use Cloud performance diagnosis to separate preview scheduler capacity, actual HTTP cost limits and database work. Four covering indexes and genuine status-table statistics have now been installed through the native writer in the reference Cloud 9.6 session. Exact typed query results, schema scope and closed resources were verified; actual application plans confirm the photo-ID route. Representative native SQL checks improved from seconds to milliseconds, with write-cost and cache-state limits documented.

One private startup renewal has now completed after a normal restart, with native commit/close and restoration of its own temporary pause. Its first held attempt remains preserved; future-launch reliability and public Cloud automation remain separate. A budget-twenty HTTP trial produced ten simultaneous cost-two tasks, but its longer observed download rate stayed near the earlier baseline (about 45 versus 44 previews/minute). More concurrency did not establish a material sustained speedup. Preserve pending requests, stop new admissions before a maintenance pause, retain rollback copies and do not confuse a faster query or returned proxy with complete Classic/cloud Sync.

Correction (2026-10-21). That native-writer renewal held one write transaction for about 40 seconds. Cloud’s own index writers give up after about 5 seconds, so they logged hundreds of “database is locked” errors, and the grid, loupe filmstrip and trash views stopped updating until restart. No data was damaged, but don’t use that method. The next recipe replaces it.
